solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Directly organise search with wife lost

indicators.note: to organise things is to put them in a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to set up a search party now that someone's wife has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' only joins the pieces: the anagram fodder is SEARCH, WIFE and LOST together, fourteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes travelling in a straight line, the shortest route, so it is a synonym of directly.

clue.text: Hot soldiers climbing trees excited tourist

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the letters go upwards, read in reverse order

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

indicators.note: excited things are stirred up, so the letters of the next word are jumbled

explanation.surface: Overheated troops scrambling up trees, watched by an excited visitor.
explanation.definitionFit: A tourist is someone out seeing the sights of a place, which is exactly what this word names.

clue.text: Race male to see where females are

parts.note: to hare is to race along at speed

explanation.surface: A man rushes off to find out where the women are gathered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Race' looks like a noun, but it is the verb, as in to hare off.
explanation.definitionFit: A harem is the women's quarters of a traditional household, a place set apart for the women.

clue.text: Boat charts army abroad regularly with navy

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every other letter of the phrase, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A boat used to map waters for an army serving overseas alongside the navy.
explanation.definitionFit: A catamaran is a type of vessel with two parallel hulls, so it is an example of a boat.

clue.text: Hunter stringing up black French duck

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so the zero-shaped letter O

indicators.note: in a down clue, stringing something up hoists it, so the letters run bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: noir is the French word for black

explanation.surface: A hunter strings up a black duck he has shot in France.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a batsman out for no runs has made a duck.
explanation.definitionFit: Orion is the hunter of Greek mythology, placed among the stars as a constellation.

clue.text: Diagram of fine church among vulgar drawings?

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads

indicators.note: among means placed in the midst of the other letters, so the church letters go inside

parts.note: low art is crude, popular art, such as vulgar drawings

explanation.surface: Questions whether a sketch of a fine church belongs among crude pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: A flowchart is a chart showing the steps of a process with boxes and arrows, a type of diagram.

clue.text: Jeremy possibly working to block NY tax collectors

indicators.note: to block is to sit in the way, inside the other letters

parts.note: the IRS (Internal Revenue Service) is the US tax authority; New York stands for the US here
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: An actor at work stands in the way of New York tax officials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' marks that Jeremy is just one person with this surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeremy Irons is a well-known English actor, so his given name is a hint to the surname.

clue.text: Right vehicle in place to get help

indicators.note: in means these letters go inside the other word

parts.note: to set something is to place it
a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Putting the correct vehicle in position to receive assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: Domestic staff are often called the help, and a servant is one such household worker.

clue.text: Copied English chapter on dictionary

parts.note: the OED is the Oxford English Dictionary

explanation.surface: An English chapter based on a dictionary that has been plagiarised.
explanation.definitionFit: To echo someone is to repeat or imitate what they said, so echoed means imitated or repeated.

clue.text: Hamlet maybe disastrous without lead on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection shows a mirror image, so the letters are read backwards
without its lead means losing the first letter

parts.note: a tragic event is a disastrous one

explanation.surface: Musing that Shakespeare's Hamlet, thought over, is a disaster without its leading actor.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet is the Shakespeare play but also a UK brand of small cigar.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet is a well-known British brand of mild cigar, so a Hamlet is an example.

clue.text: Scowl after brief prank with old Jack

indicators.note: after means the scowl word comes after the others
brief means cut short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a trick is a prank
to lour is to frown or scowl

explanation.surface: Someone frowns after a quick prank played with an old sailor named Jack.
explanation.walkthrough: A jack is a flag flown at a ship's bow, as in the Union Jack.
explanation.definitionFit: A tricolour is a three-striped national flag, and a jack is a flag, so this is an example.

clue.text: Best drug cut with end bits of talcum separately

indicators.note: separately says the pair of end letters is split up, each going into the drug at its own point
a drug cut with something has it mixed in, so these letters go inside

parts.note: opium is a narcotic drug

indicators.note: the end bits of the word talcum are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: The best drug is one cut with some talcum powder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'separately' matters: the two end letters of talcum do not go in as a pair but at two different points in the drug.
explanation.definitionFit: The optimum is the most favourable condition or amount, the best possible.

clue.text: Capital one sunk into struggling casino

indicators.note: sunk into means pushed inside the other letters
something struggling is in disarray, so its letters are scrambled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A gambler's money has gone into a casino that is going under.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of CASINO is NICOSA, with I put in near the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicosia is the capital city of Cyprus.

clue.text: Yankee nerd with dope cycling back to pub

indicators.note: cycling moves a letter round from one end of the word to the other, here last to first

parts.note: weed is slang for cannabis, also called dope

indicators.note: the back of the word is its final letter

explanation.surface: An American nerd cycles back to the pub with some dope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yankee' belongs to the definition: the word is US slang. 'back to pub' is only the final letter of pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Dweeb is American slang for a socially awkward, studious person, much the same as a nerd.

clue.text: A Christian touring island city

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the actor's surname wraps around the island

parts.note: Christian Bale is a film actor, so a Christian could be a Bale
Timor is an island in Southeast Asia

explanation.surface: A believer is on a tour of an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Christian' looks like a believer, but it is the first name of the actor Christian Bale.
explanation.definitionFit: Baltimore is a large port city in the US state of Maryland.

clue.text: Raw fish inside of fete for VIP treatment

parts.note: sore, raw skin is red
a carp is a freshwater fish

indicators.note: the inside of a word is its middle letters, without the ends

explanation.surface: Uncooked fish served at the heart of a fete as special treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Rolling out the red carpet is the idiom for giving an important guest a lavish welcome.

clue.text: Repackage third cape that's going for a snip

indicators.note: to repackage is to wrap up in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wrapping a third cape again, one that is being sold off cheaply.
explanation.walkthrough: A snip is British slang for a bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extremely cheap is a bargain, or a snip, in informal British speech.

clue.text: Case of alcohol and of grease both upended

parts.note: port is a fortified wine, an alcoholic drink

indicators.note: both says that the reversal applies to each of the two words separately
in a down clue, upended means turned upside down, so read bottom to top

parts.note: oil is a grease or lubricant

explanation.surface: A case of drink comes with some upside-down grease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'both upended' reverses OF and OIL each on its own, giving FO and LIO.
explanation.definitionFit: A portfolio is a flat case for carrying papers or drawings.

clue.text: Complicated vessel, one with a fixed course?

parts.note: something hard is difficult or complicated
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: A tricky boat that sticks to a set route.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: a liner keeps a fixed course, and a hardliner a fixed position.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardliner holds rigid views and will not change policy, like a ship that never deviates.

clue.text: Drone beat pedestrian

parts.note: to drone is to make a low hum
to drum is to beat a rhythm

explanation.surface: A droning sound beats a walker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pedestrian' looks like a walker, but here it is the adjective meaning dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedestrian as an adjective means dull and ordinary, the same sense as humdrum.

clue.text: Holy scroll I see to the right of Mount

indicators.note: in an across clue, to the right means placed after

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill or mount
ah is the exclamation of understanding, like I see

explanation.surface: Someone spots a sacred scroll on the right side of a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a rocky hilltop, especially on Dartmoor in England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Torah is the scroll of Jewish scripture read in synagogue, a sacred text.

clue.text: German guy probably reversed second carriage

parts.note: Hans is a common German man's name

indicators.note: reversed means the letters run in the opposite order

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A German man probably backed up his second car.
explanation.definitionFit: A hansom cab was a two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage.

clue.text: Exaggerate version of Fagin in Moody's clothes?

indicators.note: in means placed inside the outer letters

parts.note: the clothes of a word are its outer letters, first and last of Moody

indicators.note: a version of something is a reworking, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dressing Fagin in Ron Moody's costume overplays the character.
explanation.walkthrough: Ron Moody played Fagin in the film Oliver!, hence the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To magnify something is to make it seem bigger or more important than it is, to overstate it.

clue.text: Huge Tatar provides accommodation for nag

indicators.note: to accommodate is to house something, so the answer is held within these words

explanation.surface: A huge Tatar gives lodging to an old horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nag' looks like a horse; here it is the verb to pester.
explanation.definitionFit: To get at someone is to criticise or pick on them repeatedly, which is to nag.

clue.text: Keep heading north to catch eastern poet

indicators.note: to catch is to hold inside, so the letter goes within
in a down clue, heading north means going upwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: to stay is to keep or remain

explanation.surface: Hold course northwards to pick up an eastern poet.
explanation.definitionFit: W. B. Yeats was a celebrated Irish poet and Nobel laureate.

clue.text: Fabric bird with 50% off (no returns)

indicators.note: losing half means the second half of the word is dropped

parts.note: the chiffchaff is a small warbler

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the letters run backwards

explanation.surface: Fabric showing a bird, sold at half price with no refunds.
explanation.walkthrough: The chiffchaff is a common European warbler named after its two-note song.
explanation.definitionFit: Chiffon is a light, sheer fabric of silk or nylon.

clue.text: Suffer in short treatment

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a cure is a course of medical treatment

explanation.surface: Someone undergoes a brief course of therapy.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a loss or penalty is to bring it upon yourself and so suffer it.

clue.text: Reason allotment has beer

parts.note: a ration is an allotted portion
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: The reason a share includes beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'allotment' suggests a vegetable plot, but here it is a share handed out.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the underlying reasoning or justification for an action.

clue.text: What Ma plays from some contrary collection

indicators.note: contrary means going the opposite way, so the letters are read backwards
some of means only part of the word is used

explanation.surface: Wondering what Mum plays from an assortment of contrary pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: Ma is Yo-Yo Ma, the famous cellist, not a mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Yo-Yo Ma is a world-renowned cellist, so his instrument is the one he plays.

clue.text: Abbess in car crossing the lady's lovely isle

indicators.note: crossing means stretched across, so the car letters straddle the others

parts.note: a motor is a car
her is the possessive pronoun for a lady
super means lovely or excellent
I is the abbreviation for isle, as on maps

explanation.surface: An abbess drives across her beautiful island in a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mother Superior is the head nun of a convent, the title held by an abbess.
